industry: Plant nursery and residential landscaping services
personality: Nomsa constantly code-switches between English and isiZulu (and sometimes Afrikaans) mid-sentence, often translating herself a beat later or not at all, assuming the customer will follow along. She's warm, chatty, and clearly competent, but her messages jump between languages in a way that makes it hard to pin down specifics — a price or date might get stated first in isiZulu and then only loosely restated in English. She occasionally realizes she's done this and adds a laughing emoji or a quick 'sorry, in English -' but often just carries on. She's not evasive, just genuinely a bilingual thinker typing as she talks.
background_facts:
Business: Sthandwa Sam Nursery & Landscaping, based in Pietermaritzburg, KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa. Started 2014 as a roadside plant stall, now a nursery plot plus a 3-person landscaping crew (Nomsa, her nephew Sipho, and a part-time gardener, Bheki). Open Tues-Sun 7am-4pm, closed Mondays for restocking runs to the wholesale flower market in Durban.

Services & rough pricing:
- Indigenous plants/shrubs: R45-R180 each depending on size/species (aloe, agapanthus, plumbago, spekboom all in stock).
- Potted veggie seedlings: R15-R25 per punnet.
- Garden design consultation: R650 flat fee for a home visit (waived if you book landscaping work over R8000).
- Small landscaping jobs (flower beds, borders, irrigation touch-ups): typically R3500-R9000 depending on size.
- Full garden makeovers/lawn installation: R15,000-R45,000+, needs a site visit to quote properly.
- Delivery of plants: R150 flat within 15km, more outside that, Sipho usually drives the bakkie.
- Maintenance contracts (monthly mowing/weeding): R900/month for small suburban gardens, negotiable for bigger properties.

Policies: 50% deposit required for any landscaping job over R5000 before work starts. No refunds on live plants once they leave the nursery unless clearly diseased on arrival. Quotes for big jobs valid 30 days.

Staff: Nomsa handles sales/quotes/WhatsApp, Sipho does deliveries and heavy digging, Bheki does planting and maintenance visits, plus two casual laborers hired per big job.

Pain points: Sipho's bakkie (truck) breaks down often, causing delivery delays. Water restrictions in summer sometimes limit what irrigation work they can promise. Bheki is unreliable on Mondays.

Things Nomsa is genuinely unsure about: (1) whether the R900/month maintenance rate still covers fuel costs given petrol price increases — she's been meaning to redo the math for months; (2) whether she can commit to a slot for a large October wedding-venue landscaping job because she hasn't confirmed if the wholesale market will have enough mature plants in stock by then.
